chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar, who said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad and Muḥammad ibn al-Walīd narrated to us, from Yūnus ibn Yaʿqūb, from Manṣūr ibn Ḥāzim, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
My father fell ill on the Day of al-Aḍḥā, so he performed two rakʿahs in his house, then he offered the sacrifice.

Thus, the proper approach regarding these reports is that we interpret them as indicating a kind of recommendation, because this prayer with the Imam is obligatory, while when performed individually it is an emphasized sunnah (prophetic tradition); and that which indicates this is:

key_terms.الِاسْتِحْبَابِ: recommendation; the legal interpretation applied to these reports
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the Imam, with whom the Eid prayer is considered obligatory
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْنِ: two units of prayer performed in the home
key_terms.سُنَّةٌ مُؤَكَّدَةٌ: an emphasized sunnah (prophetic tradition); the ruling when performed individually
key_terms.ضَحَّى: offered the sacrifice associated with Eid al-Aḍḥā
key_terms.فَرْضٌ: obligatory; the ruling of the prayer when with the Imam
key_terms.مَرِضَ: fell ill; indicating the circumstance that prevented public attendance
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْأَضْحَى: the Day of al-Aḍḥā, the occasion of the Eid prayer and sacrifice

ai.seo_question: Is Eid prayer obligatory only with the Imam, and what is its ruling when prayed individually?
ai.summary: This report relates that the father of Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, due to illness on the Day of al-Aḍḥā, performed two rakʿahs in his home and then offered the sacrifice. The accompanying legal statement explains that such reports are understood to indicate recommendation for the Eid prayer when performed individually, while its performance with the Imam is considered obligatory.
